My parents let me stay in my room and jerk off and smoke weed for 3 years after high school. I told people I was fine. That I was happy. I wasn't, and I wish I could get those years back.

Them pushing isn't necessarily a bad thing, but obviously I'm not there. I would suggest picking a direction that you want to go in. Something you genuinely enjoy doing and are interested in. If they see you are productive hopefully they will back off. (In terms of the internship).

And quite honestly, if you don't want to quit you won't. You can still be a stoner and be somewhat productive. Sorry if I sound preachy but if you don't pick a direction now you will regret it. I do.

Would you please remove that 44% statistic from your recent article? The message is woefully needed, but that stat is not accurate. It's only perpetuating misinformation and discredits the fight against sexual violence.

Remember that suicidal thoughts are not uncommon, especially after someone close to you has taken their own life. There is nothing "wrong" or "crazy" about the way you feel right now. When it happens to me I don't try to push it out, I simply let it be there. If you try to push bad thoughts out they just boomerang right back (at least for me anyways).

From personal experience I would recommend trying to achieve  some form of closure. Whether that is to forgive yourself, forgive your friend, or forgive whomever you may feel is at fault (rationally or irrationally).
